title: fix: honor the gateway probe overall timeout
body:
Closes #127166

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `gateway probe --timeout` exceeding its advertised overall budget when discovery is slow or finds many Gateways.

## User Impact

Known local and explicit Gateways are checked while discovery runs. Discovery, SSH configuration and tunnel setup, connections, and read checks share one deadline, and unfinished checks report a timeout. Existing options and standalone discovery behavior are preserved; no migration is needed. Connection and process cleanup can briefly extend elapsed command time.

## Why This Change Was Made

On the integrated main base (`431f80cf7ac4`), `src/commands/gateway-status.ts:135` resolves SSH configuration before cancellation exists, `:232` waits for discovery before probing known targets, and `:308` gives probes a fresh budget. `src/infra/bonjour-discovery.ts:264` also restarts the timeout for each DNS-SD resolution.

The command owns one monotonic deadline and cancellation signal. Its existing discovery, SSH, and probe owners consume the remaining budget. Direct checks on the tunnel's preferred loopback port finish before the tunnel can bind it, preserving credential routing. Main's consolidation in `32e8d817f7d1` is retained: SSH resolution and auto-discovery remain in the command, and the deleted `gateway-status/discovery.ts` is not restored. No additional timeout manager, fallback, or public option is introduced.

Against the integrated main base: production +229/-153 (net +76), tests +136/-6 (net +130), documentation +5/-0. The added production code supports concurrent checks and cancellation through the existing owners.

## Evidence

Three regressions fail against main's production code and pass with the fix: DNS-SD resolves a third beacon after the deadline; known healthy targets remain unprobed during slow discovery; and the SSH tunnel starts before same-port direct checks finish. The tunnel regression uses controlled promises.

All 42 tests pass across `gateway-status.test.ts`, `bonjour-discovery.test.ts`, and `ssh-config.test.ts` via the repository runner with one worker. The full focused wrapper took 67.53 seconds, including compiler preparation (infra shard 46.84 seconds; command shard 8.23 seconds). Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Independent Codex review reports scoped-clean with no actionable P0-P2 findings.

No live network or SSH endpoint was used, per this repair lane's focused-proof scope. Owner-level regressions exercise deadline and ordering behavior; exact-head PR CI supplies broad validation. Exact-head CI run [39639655335](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39639655335) passed on `3d84106ff8d9f5909fb573dfa8295a8583ca46ac`: 33 jobs passed, with no failing or pending jobs; the repository watcher returned `GREEN`. Runner queueing caused most of the delay; no CI rerun or follow-up fix was needed. Superseded review-orchestration checks remain visible in GitHub's aggregate rollup and are excluded by the repository watcher.

ClawSweeper re-review was requested once on this head and observed through the 25-minute window. Its automatic attempts did not publish a current-head review; [run 39644119762](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/39644119762) subsequently reported that no publishable artifact was produced. The visible review still covers the previous head. This is a review-infrastructure gap, not a claim of a clean current-head ClawSweeper review; the independent review above is complete.
